title: #257: Reality Fracture State of the Format Address
scale: Letter grades (A+ to F), the same scale as the show's set review and tier list

format.summary: A highly balanced, powerful, and complex set where nearly every card has a home; you must draft decks rather than cards, and 17lands averages are less reliable for low-rated synergy cards. The Empower Jace mechanic is praised as superbly tuned.
format.speed: Slow and grindy: early creatures attack poorly, boards stabilize around turn five or six, and the winner is usually whoever keeps spending mana well late. Aggro exists only in niches such as blue-white and heavy red.

colors.take: Its best plan is going wide with 2/2 tokens plus team pumps rather than traditional beatdown.
Excellent card draw and strong counterspells, which shine against expensive enters-the-battlefield threats and planeswalkers.
Efficient removal and graveyard recursion; the sacrifice support is thin.
Very strong removal throughout, plus a viable pinging aggro plan if you are nearly mono-red in an open seat.
The base for ramp and graveyard decks; Heartwood tokens make splashing red especially easy.

pairs.take: One of the best decks: aggressive surveil and go-wide with cheap flyers; easy to draft and good for learning the format.
His favorite deck: mill flashback cards and recur high-value enters-the-battlefield creatures with Rewrite Regrets.
The base for multicolor ramp, often splashing removal or card draw to reach Crusher and Kiora.
Lowest win rate on 17lands because its sacrifice theme lacks pieces, but it works as go-wide plus black removal.
The most aggressive pair on paper, though black adds little to red aggro beyond a few gold cards.
Its life-gain theme often ends up as a go-wide deck instead.

mechanics.name: Empower Jace
mechanics.take: Brilliantly balanced. Attack an opposing Jace at three or more loyalty, protect your own at three, and usually cash in three loyalty for a card, surveilling instead only in specific spots.

mechanics.name: Way enchantments
mechanics.take: Wildly uneven. Healer and Mind Sculptor are top tier, Paradox is close behind, Mentor and Necromancer are unplayable, and they stack poorly, so run about three at most.

mechanics.name: Land cycling / fixing
mechanics.take: Excellent fixing, from duals that enter untapped with a planeswalker, Murmuring Volume, and strong landcyclers, makes splashing easy, even double-pip splashes with seven or eight sources.

mechanics.name: Flashback / graveyard
mechanics.take: Well supported in black-green with mill enablers and recursion of value creatures.

advice: Never run out of things to do with your mana; avoid too many two-drops and cards with no late-game role.
Play about six or seven removal spells in midrange decks, value removal that hits planeswalkers, and count counterspells as removal.
Include three or four cards that put you up a card, fewer if you have lots of Empower Jace.
Splash off-color removal or card draw freely, adding an extra tapped dual land or two.
Speculate on landcyclers and dual lands fairly highly, even fourth pick in a weak pack.
Save removal for the many must-answer threats rather than spending it on tokens.
Think in terms of synergy packages rather than strict color-pair archetypes, adding colors for synergy pieces.
